source_title: Kolkata Police launches probe after man in Denmark gets three traffic challans in three months - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Kolkata: A man, who has been in Denmark for three months, received a traffic challan in Kolkata for riding a scooterette without a helmet . He said his two-wheeler was locked at his home and could not have been used as he was away.The traffic rule violation ticket claimed the offence took place at the APC Roy Road-Shibdas Bhaduri Street crossing at 5.50 am on Oct 19. In his post on X, while the man asked Kolkata Police to correct the mistake, he also pointed out that the payment website was not opening.The person reportedly received similar challans twice earlier in the same period, when he was in Denmark.Kolkata Police asked him to send them his complaint by email and senior Lalbazar officers said they would investigate whether the message was real or caused by human error. An office said many such cases turned out to be fake SMS messages that looked like official e-challans. In some cases, he said, the vehicleâs ownership details were not updated and so, challan messages were sent to old owners though the vehicle might have been sold off to someone else.Police are also worried about duplicate or fake registration numbers. They may take up the matter with RTOs.Lalbazar had earlier launched an investigation after bus and minibus owners complained that some sergeants issued fines of small amounts without entering the payments in the official system. Police said they now handled such complaints more carefully. A team, led by a DCP, currently reviews complaints, and in some genuine cases, cancels fines.
